overview.label: Story
overview.heading: Overview
overview.body: An exploration of real-time interactive 3D on the web — prototyping spatial interaction models, lighting, and motion tuned for performance, to find the patterns that make 3D feel like a native part of an interface rather than a novelty.

problem.label: Problem
problem.heading: Why this needed to exist
problem.body: 3D on the web often feels gimmicky — latency, missing affordance, and heavy assets break presence and make it feel bolted-on.

approach.label: Approach
approach.heading: How the work got done
approach.body: Prototyped real-time 3D environments, iterating on spatial interaction models, lighting, and motion to keep everything responsive and performant in the browser.

outcomes.label: Outcomes
outcomes.heading: What changed once it shipped
outcomes.body: A set of reusable spatial interaction patterns for interactive 3D that feel native — turning 3D from a novelty into a usable medium.

credits.label: Credits
credits.heading: One last thing
credits.body: Real-time interactive 3D — spatial interaction models, lighting, and motion prototyped for the web, built to feel native rather than gimmicky.
